synthesis.answer: The passages point to the Kawasaki Ninja H2 as a leading candidate, but they disagree on which bike is fastest. The supporting sources call the Ninja H2 one of the strongest candidates for India's fastest production motorcycle, and say it sits near the top of the speed list [e3effe5ed347#2] [e3effe5ed347#3]. The contradicting sources add nuance: the Kawasaki Ninja H2R reaches nearly 400 km/h but is track-only and not road-legal in India [5bab82194822#2] [0d96b47079bb#1]. Among road-legal bikes, the Ducati Panigale V4 R is described as exceeding 330 km/h with a race exhaust [5bab82194822#5] [5bab82194822#2], while the Ninja H2 SX SE is listed at 330 km/h top speed [0618079a2be5#0]. The BMW M 1000 RR is homologated to about 314 km/h [5bab82194822#6]. Many sources also cite a 299 km/h cap shared by several superbikes [0618079a2be5#1]. Overall, the H2R is the fastest production bike overall, but among road-legal bikes the Panigale V4 R or Ninja H2 are the contenders, with the evidence roughly balanced.
synthesis.one_line: Kawasaki Ninja H2R is fastest overall but track-only; among road-legal bikes, Ducati Panigale V4 R or Ninja H2 lead, sources disagree.
